body:
For the record, this was added in #71437 by @vaartis, but I researched it again to understand better in which case it's actually needed. We might want to reconsider this override.

It seems like dwarf-5 is the new default since GCC 11, but it depends on GNU binutils version 2.35 for `addr2line` to support it.

https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-11/changes.html
https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/BINUTILS235

From a quick look at https://pkgs.org/download/binutils, the only supported Linux distro that doesn't have at least binutils 2.35 is Ubuntu 20.04, which is still on 2.34.

Maybe losing support for backtraces on Ubuntu 20.04 is a reasonable compromise now to have the latest dwarf format, which according to GCC release notes "can produce up to 25% more compact debug information compared to earlier versions."

Now, this was originally reported on #devel by @adamscott in Jan 2023 and I doubt that he was running Ubuntu 20.04 at the time, so that's weird.

We should also evaluate whether macOS could use `dwarf-5` too.

> Now, this was originally reported on #devel by @adamscott in Jan 2023 and I doubt that he was running Ubuntu 20.04 at the time, so that's weird.

I was running contemporary Fedora.

So I just realized - while running into it - that this can lead to loading wrong debugsymbols if you have a `.debugsymbols` file laying around from a previous build.

This can happen if you build with `separate_debug_symbols=yes` once, and then not afterwards, or if the debugsymbols are bigger than 2 GiB (which forces separate debug symbols) for a build, and then dip back under 2 GiB afterwards (which makes it default to keeping debug symbols in the binary).

These shouldn't be too frequent scenarios but this still seems brittle, and especially annoying if the main `.exe` actually contains debugsymbols but this piece of code forces it to load invalid symbols from another build.
